clinician.final_diagnosis: Parkes-Weber syndrome (confirmed by RASA1 variant Chr5(GRCh37)g.86659154_86659158del)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old woman with lifelong left thigh enlargement (roughly double the circumference of the right thigh) and capillary malformations (birthmarks) present since birth presented to the ED with 1 day of acute painful worsening described as 'tightness,' relieved by rest and aggravated by movement. Physical examination confirmed chronic asymmetry with soft compartments, normal neurovascular function, and absence of edema, erythema, or calf tenderness. Dermatology confirmed large birthmarks on the left leg and referred for suspected vascular malformations. Venography by interventional radiology revealed arteriovenous fistulas in the left thigh. Initial laboratory workup showed elevated d-dimer (3.25 μg/mL) and markedly elevated creatine kinase (7697 U/L), with normal CBC, metabolic panel, and negative pregnancy test. Lower extremity ultrasound ruled out deep vein thrombosis (patent, compressible, bilaterally symmetric femoral and popliteal veins) but showed soft tissue edema in the medial left thigh. The patient was treated with IV fluid bolus (30 mL/kg normal saline to prevent acute kidney injury), acetaminophen, and morphine for pain control. After consultation with orthopedics and nephrology, the patient was discharged home with diagnosis of rhabdomyolysis after extended ED stay, with creatine kinase trending down to 1800 U/L and clinical improvement. Genetic analysis confirmed RASA1 variant (Chr5(GRCh37)g.86659154_86659158del), establishing the definitive diagnosis of Parkes-Weber syndrome.
